audience: Trace product engineers and designers who ship selects across the app
fidelity: High-fidelity spec with annotated anatomy, states, and usage rules
primaryJob: Define one consistent Select component so every dropdown in the product looks and behaves the same
coreFlow: Read the anatomy and token spec
Check menu, item, and list behavior
Apply the usage rules to existing inconsistent selects
Try the interactive reference select in context

direction.name: Trace Web Design System
principles: Source-backed tokens from the tracev2 package (dark-only, Geist, blue accent)
One trigger recipe and one menu recipe reused everywhere
Selection is always a trailing check in a reserved slot
Restrained color: accent only for focus and selection emphasis

preserve: Trailing check for the selected item
reinterpret: Selected-row background tint becomes pointer-highlight only
Pill trigger unifies with the 6px-radius field recipe
avoidCopying: Trace product copy and palette icon

reinterpret: Submenus belong to DropdownMenu, not Select
Breadcrumb-style trigger value standardizes to a single label
avoidCopying: Third-party product names as spec content
evidence: Check floats mid-row next to a submenu chevron
Row height ~52px, larger than sibling menus

reinterpret: Trigger value must match the item label exactly (menu shows Member, trigger shows lowercase member)
Check moves from beside the label into the reserved trailing slot
evidence: Trigger is a pill while the popup is a rounded rect

reinterpret: Scroll chevron becomes the standard scroll button with a fade edge
evidence: Selected row uses a lighter persistent fill

assumptions: Control-level state coverage (placeholder, value, hover, focus-visible, open, disabled, invalid, item highlight/selected/disabled/destructive, scrollable list) renders inside the 'All states' spec sheets rather than as separate artboards
The four screenshots are current product selects supplied as evidence of inconsistency, not styles to copy
Spec targets the source app's Base UI Select recipe (components.manifest.json: sizes sm/default, aria-invalid, data-placeholder)
Geist Variable is the product font; the canvas renders its sans-serif fallback since no local font file ships in this workspace
Muted (#71717a to #90909a) and danger (#ef4444 to #f87171) text roles are raised on these artboards so all text meets 4.5:1 AA; the spec recommends the product adopt the same values for dark surfaces
Desktop-first: artboards are spec sheets at 1200px-wide viewports
